materials.verdict: The smooth look is mostly not texture resolution; the worst offender is the water. On a real GPU in the web build the river is one flat off-white sheet (mean RGB 206,203,202, luminance std 1.4 to 1.9 of 255 across 1400x370 px, versus 9.8 for the lawn beside it). It has a razor-straight near edge, no foam and no tint, and it reads as a concrete slab. Cause: water.gdshader sets ROUGHNESS 0.04 and SPECULAR 0.8, so at grazing angles it mirrors the pale horizon and the dark body colour is lost. The owner's screenshot-1 "white raised slab with stepped edge" is the SIDEWALK under a low sun, covered in shadow-map staircase banding. I reproduced it in the web build at 16:48 (road and sidewalk both show terraced diagonal bands and a stair-stepped shadow edge), so it is lighting, not texture. The web caps (ground 1024, building normals 256, ARM 128) are not the cause: at 0.6 scale a pixel covers 2.7 mm per metre of distance against 2.9 mm per texel of the 3 m grass tile, so the 2048 source would show detail only inside about 1.5 m. There is no sand, rock or snow terrain at all (the sim has only land and water), so sand cannot look different because it does not exist. The lawn, asphalt and concrete slabs are low-contrast, single-texture surfaces that vanish at 0.6 scale with SSAO off. The best fix per byte is shader work: water v2, lawn and asphalt contrast, a shore band, and a shadow-bias fix, with about 5 MB of dead textures removed to pay for it. artifacts.verdict: Lines: reproduced and root-caused on the web build (headless Chrome, real GPU, stock code plus a scratch debug hook). In clear weather at 10:45 the road and sidewalk carry fine, tilted and curved stripes that are sun shadow-map acne (street sun normal bias 0.6 with the web tier's 1024 atlas). Normal bias 2.0 or depth bias 0.2, sun off, shadow reach 0, or roads/sidewalks not casting all remove them. They are absent in overcast weather and are NOT SSAO (SSAO is correctly off in the web build). The 83fe2e8 fix raised the normal bias only while aerial, and its row-profile metric is blind to tilted/curved stripes. Legs: reproduced the mechanism, not the exact screenshot. The hero has one y for the whole body (centre-point sampling, no per-foot ground fit), so standing at a 12 cm kerb with the centre on the low side buries the high-side foot and hides the shoe (seen in a close-up render). Lot tiles also use flat collision heights while the meshes have slabs and sloped aprons (code reading plus a partial headless scan). Not checked: desktop build, which build the owner ran, the finer bias sweep (run killed before it ran). The report file could not be written (the tool refused it); the full findings are here and the evidence images and scripts are in the scratch dir.

carentry.verdict: The pull-out is real but too fast and too loosely coupled to the hero to read as a hold-and-drag. The grab, the 0.4 s haul and the 0.4 s fall are only about 0.8 s long, the hands touch the driver for about 0.2 s, and the driver's torso passes within 4 to 7 cm of the hero's root. "Sudden sit" is real. The main mechanism is in drive_feature.gd: a failed walk to the door, or a blocked door or sill, ejects the driver and seats the hero in the same frame with no grab. Three more paths skip the pull: a driver with no drawn body or no sidewalk to run to, buses and trucks (never pulled), and the action hijack (no hero grip). I checked desktop only (headless probes and one Vulkan window), not the web build.

water.verdict: The hero cannot enter water because open-water tiles return NAN from CollisionWorld.ground_height(), and every stand/step/is_blocked check treats NAN as a wall; I reproduced this headless (hero stops exactly at the tile border, x=25.5000, even sprinting). The river is only 1.0 m deep (bed -1.6 m, surface -0.6 m), so wading is cheap to allow: a prototype with a hero-only wade_max param let the hero walk about 3 m into the river and stop at 0.79 m depth, with no change for NPCs, cars or animals. Separately, on the web build the river renders as a flat pale grey-white slab like cement (measured RGB 200,199,192, stddev 2.4: no ripples, foam or depth tint), very probably what the owner calls cement and smooth. A scratch web export proved the cause: the water shader's depth read uses the Forward+ unprojection but web runs gl_compatibility, so the original shader outputs t_depth=0, foam=1 everywhere (all foam); a one-line NDC change gives dark rippled water with a foam ring round the pole. There is no swim or wade clip in the animation library, so the plan is wade-only (about 0.8 m max) using the existing walk clips and the existing footstep_splash sounds. NOTE: the tool refused to write report.md (subagents may not write report files), so the full report is in this structured output.

audio.verdict: The web build is silent for every player, whatever the browser, volume or autoplay setting. It is a code and engine-interaction bug, not a missing file, browser policy or an owner mute. Godot 4.7.2 plays web audio in Sample mode, which mixes through a JS Web Audio bus graph. When audio_feature._make_buses() calls AudioServer.add_bus() four times at first-person start, the engine disconnects Master's output node from the AudioContext destination and wires it into the SFX bus. SFX -> Music -> Master already feed Master, so the graph is also a cycle. Buffers decode and start (40+ sources, non-zero gains) but the destination peak is exactly 0.0 for the whole session. Reconnecting that one node live took the peak from 0 to 0.19-0.66. A patched pack with a default bus layout, or with Stream playback on web, is audible from boot. The live site serves release 7588ac5d7c80bf51, the build I tested. Checked: the web build in headless Chrome 151 on software WebGL with no --mute-audio. I read desktop audio from code only; it is unlikely to be affected because it uses the C++ mixer. The browser autoplay policy was not reproduced. I could not get a suspended context in headless Chrome, so a visible click-to-enable prompt is a precaution, not a proven cause. The Write tool refused the report file in this harness, so the full report is in this structured result and report_path points to a file that does not exist.

root_causes.title: Master bus output is disconnected from the AudioContext destination when buses are added at runtime in web Sample playback mode
root_causes.evidence: Instrumented AudioContext (probe.js), local image 0528316, policy document-user-activation-required, no --mute-audio. Control runs (run-noauto, run-pol, run-graph): ctx 'running', 40-46 AudioBufferSource starts with maxabs 0.38-0.95, non-zero channel gains (0.63, 0.03...), destination peak 0.0 from boot to +62 s. The op log shows 4 bus creations at page-time 5.6 s, each followed by 'disconnect master mute node (id 5)' then 'connect 5 -> SFX bus input (27)'. Final graph: master -> SFX(27), SFX(29) -> Music(24), Ambience and UI -> SFX, Music(26) -> Master(3): a cycle with no edge to the destination. Repair test in the same run: master.disconnect(); master.connect(ctx.destination) gave peak 0.19, 0.57, 0.30, 0.66 within 6 s. The JS (index.js) shows Bus.connect() calls getOutputNode().disconnect() first, and set_sample_bus_send() falls back to a target bus when the index is invalid. The C++ call that passes the wrong send index is inferred, not read from engine source.

VERDICT. Measured on a REAL GPU: Chrome 151 headless, WebGL renderer 'ANGLE (AMD, AMD Radeon Graphics (radeonsi renoir ACO), OpenGL ES 3.2)' (the AMD Renoir iGPU, not SwiftShader), build kunalsiyag1/gridfall-web:0528316 run in the local container (threads true, crossOriginIsolated true, 8 pthread workers), 1600x900, DPR 1, flags --disable-frame-rate-limit --disable-gpu-vsync (a clearing canvas ran at 10,000 fps, so the 60 Hz cap is gone for light frames). The web build is CPU-bound on one main thread, not GPU-bound. Four separate causes make it 'not smooth', in order of felt impact:
(1) BLOCKING SHADER COMPILES: 467 programs / 25.3 s of synchronous linkProgram/compileShader waits in a 2.5 min session on a cold cache. 206 programs / 11.4 s sit inside the boot's first draw (75% of the 15.3 s boot); 261 programs / 13.8 s hit later as first-use freezes (start walking 0.36-0.45 s; rain/lamp pool ~1.0 s; first Tab overview 1.7-1.8 s; Quit to orbit 3.2-4.6 s; back to street 1-4.6 s). Nothing warms them up. Per program: median 37 ms, p90 150 ms, max 213 ms; each Godot Compatibility program is ~34 KB vertex + ~90 KB fragment GLSL; 81 distinct shader bodies expand to 460 programs (~5.7 variants each).
(2) THE PLANNER (orbit) VIEW: 19-25 fps (cb p50 29 ms day 1, 40-45 ms day 10; GPU 22-26 ms), 8k (day 1) to 22k (day 10) draws and 35-37 million vertices per frame, ignores the web quality tier (identical at Low/Medium/High), and freezes 540-670 ms three times per 12 s on day 10 (pure CPU, no GL: unsliced whole sim ticks) plus an autosave per 12 s game day.
(3) GROWN-CITY STREET (day 10): main-thread p50 15.1 ms, p95 19.6, ~4.5% of frames over 34 ms (a missed 60 Hz vsync), ~56 fps; traffic+pedestrians cost 2.5 ms, animals 1.0 ms; the audio feature causes the slow-frame tail; 16% (day 10) to 28% (day 1) of the main thread is blocked in two synchronous GL calls per frame that wait for the browser GPU process.
(4) TRANSITIONS: Quit to orbit freezes the screen 2.7-4.2 s, Tab back 3.5-3.9 s.
GPU time is NOT the limit in first person on this machine (3.2-4.8 ms/frame); it is the limit in the Planner (22-26 ms). The Low/Medium/High picker is nearly decorative on web: Quality.WEB overrides scale, atlas, view range, LOD and lights for every tier.

HONEST LIMITS of this measurement. Intervals still cluster at 16.7 and 33.4 ms on game frames (p50 ~16, p95 ~34 on the grown street), so presentation stays quantised to 60 Hz multiples downstream of the main thread; trust cb (rAF callback ms) and gpu (EXT_disjoint_timer_query_webgl2 ms) over fps. Headless has no real compositor/display: it cannot say how a headed Chrome at 60 or 144 Hz (the owner's notes say the droid measured on a 144 Hz display), VRR, battery throttling or another GPU/driver paces the same frames. A 15 ms frame on 144 Hz is 2.2 vsyncs, i.e. 13.9/20.8 ms alternation (judder) without VRR. 3x-slower-GPU implication (INFERRED from the CPU/GPU split): first-person street stays CPU-bound (GPU 3.2-4.8 -> ~10-14 ms vs 9.4-16 ms CPU, so ~15 -> 15-17 ms day 10, 9.6 -> 10-12 ms day 1); the Planner goes 22-26 -> 66-78 ms GPU = 13-15 fps; boot/first-use compile cost is driver CPU work (37 ms/program here) and is UNVERIFIED on Windows ANGLE/D3D11 or Intel/Apple drivers where 90 KB fragment shaders may take 100-300 ms each (boot 20-60 s, freezes 3-12 s) - the biggest unknown for the demo machine.

Sets: walking/sprint (6 programs, ~0.4 s), rain + lamp pool + beam + poster composite (~3 s), Tab overview (40-56 programs, 1.8 s), orbit/Planner (52-101 programs, 2.5-4.6 s), street return. Total compile work is unchanged (~25 s cold on this GPU), it moves it behind the veil / splits it between programs; Chrome's persistent shader cache then makes repeat visits ~4.7 s faster at boot.

fix_plan.title: 4. Apply the web render tier to the Planner view and cut its geometry
fix_plan.what: render_opt._restore() returns the viewport to project values in orbit, so the Planner renders at the full 1600x900, 22k draws (7.4k = 4 shadow cascades at 2048x2048) and 37 M vertices (35 M already on day 1). On web: scale 0.75-0.85, cap the shadow reach / cascades (aerial_shadow), far-tree LOD or impostors for the whole-map tree plant, no MSAA. GPU is vertex-bound (720p->1080p only 22->26 ms), so geometry is the lever.

fix_plan.expected_gain: Estimated (shadows are 34% of draws): ~12-15 ms of the 41-45 ms CPU and ~40% of GPU; target 30 fps on this GPU. NOT measured: no runtime switch exists.
